chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, raising it to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning salat (prayer) in pure khazz.
“There is no harm in it. But as for that in which the fur of rabbits or other such things resembling this is mixed, then do not perform salat (prayer) in it.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer) being discussed in relation to valid clothing
key_terms.الْأَرَانِبِ: rabbits, whose fur is mentioned as a disqualifying mixture
key_terms.الْخَزِّ: khazz, a type of fabric mentioned as permissible when pure
key_terms.فَلَا تُصَلِّ: do not perform salat (prayer), indicating prohibition
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm, indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in clothing made of pure khazz or mixed with rabbit fur?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about clothing worn in salat (prayer). It permits praying in pure khazz, while forbidding prayer in material mixed with rabbit fur or similar substances.
